summary: Todd T. Lewis works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University under mentors Ainslie T. Embree, Morton Klass, Theodore Riccardi Jr., and Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 1996–2017).

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He attended Akita Prefectural Akita High School and earned a geshe degree at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University, and Toyo Bunko.
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen studied under Kim Plofker from around 2003 to 2008 and under David Pingree in 2008.

Tokio Takata (born 1949) specializes in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences. His career includes posts at Otaru University of Commerce, Kyoto University, and Fudan University.

Tokiyuki Hojo (1858–1929) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). During his career, he held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1894–1896), Kanazawa University (~1898–1908), and Tohoku University (~1913–1917).

Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held positions at Komazawa University from 1949 to 1987 and as a lecturer at Eihei-ji from 1977 to 1987.

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He held posts at Fukui Normal School, Fukui Prefectural Fujishima High School, and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and at the University of Freiburg under Martin Heidegger. He held posts at Kyoto Institute of Technology, Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, Kyoto University of Education, and Ryukoku University.

Tom Tillemans (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Jacques May (~1980–1989) and served on the faculty at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018), later holding a visiting chair at the University of Calgary (~2004).

Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University (MA ~1977–1979), and UC Santa Barbara (PhD ~1979–1985). She held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–2001) and the University of Michigan (1999; ~2001–2020).
Tomoyasu Oshima works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto (attested 2012) and served as a lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine (born 1971) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and an associate professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He completed a master's at the University of Madras under C. S. Sundaram and earned a PhD at Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal, later holding a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Canterbury in 1993, studying under Paul Harrison and William Sax. He has held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2008).

Tony K. Stewart (born 1954) specializes in Indology and religious studies. After studying at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976), he held academic posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011–2021).

Torakazu Doi (1902–1971) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1923–1926) and later held positions at Sagami Women's University (~1951–1964) and Dokkyo University (~1964–1971).

Torkel Brekke (born 1970), specializing in Indology and religious studies, earned an MPhil at the University of Oslo and a doctorate at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He has held posts at PRIO, the University of Oslo, Oslo Metropolitan University, and MF Norwegian School of Theology.

Toru Funayama (born 1961) is an Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner. He held academic posts at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

Toru Haneda (1882–1955) worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the Third Higher School, University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University, he served in multiple posts at Kyoto University (1909–1948), Toho Gakkai, and the Institute of Eastern Culture.
